items.title: Labour market overview, UK: October 2026
items.method_sample: Labour Force Survey (81,193 individuals Apr-Jun 2026), HMRC PAYE RTI, Vacancy Survey

points.claim: UK vacancies fell to their lowest outside the pandemic since 2014
points.evidence: 691,000 for July to September 2026, down 21,000 (2.9%) on April to June, down 37,000 (5.1%) on the year
points.quote: 691,000 or fewer vacancies outside the COVID-19 period last seen July to September 2014 (686,000)

points.claim: Unemployment fell and employment rose even as vacancies fell
points.quote: The UK unemployment rate ... was estimated at 4.7% in June to August 2026

points.claim: Payrolled employees still falling year on year
points.evidence: down 111,000 (0.4%) Aug 2025 to Aug 2026; Sept flash 30.3 million, down 66,000 on year

items.title: REC JobsOutlook, June to August 2026
items.method_sample: Whitestone Insight survey of 704 UK employers, 15 June-18 Aug 2026, weighted by region, industry, sector

points.claim: Employer economic confidence improves but stays deeply negative
points.quote: Economic confidence rose by eight percentage points to a net balance of -39% in the June-August 2026 period.
Confidence in making hiring and investment decisions improved by six points to -8%.
Short-term permanent hiring intentions edged down one point to a net balance of +8%.

points.claim: Temp intentions flat to lower; North and Midlands lead
points.quote: The short-term net balance fell one point to +2%, while the medium-term balance remained at +5%.

items.title: SIA | Bullhorn Staffing Indicator, week ending October 10, 2026
items.method_sample: Weekly hours worked by temps across US staffing firms using Bullhorn, benchmarked to BLS

points.claim: US staffing hours at a year-to-date high
points.quote: US Staffing hours were up 11% compared to a year ago and up 0.6% on a week-over-week sequential basis
Commercial hours were up 12% compared to a year ago
Professional hours were up 9% compared to a year ago
The average weekly hours worked per worker was 35.5 hours during the week ending October 10th
